      "text": "Based on the image, this is a mod configuration menu for the game **Terraria**. The tooltip is explaining a setting related to how **Life Fruits** spawn.\n\nHere is the translation and meaning of the Chinese text:\n\n**Setting Name:**\n\u003e **生命果限制调整: 0**\n\u003e *Life Fruit Limit Adjustment: 0*\n\n**Tooltip Translation:**\n*   **可以调整生命果对于周围生命果的判断范围，数值越小生命果长得越密集**\n    *Translation:* This allows you to adjust the detection radius for surrounding Life Fruits. The smaller the value, the denser (closer together) the Life Fruits will grow.\n*   **当为-1时，则为原版限制（每隔60（普通）/ 50（专家）图格生成一个）**\n    *Translation:* When set to -1, it applies the vanilla game limit (spawns one every 60 tiles in Normal mode / 50 tiles in Expert mode).\n*   **调整时，需注意在专家及以上难度下，实际数值为该数值-10**\n    *Translation:* Please note when adjusting: in Expert difficulty and above, the actual effective value will be your set value minus 10.\n\n**What it means for your gameplay:**\nIn the base game of Terraria, Life Fruits will not spawn right next to each other; they require a certain amount of space.       "text": "how do i configure my mods or disable them to reduce this glitching in my visuals, like certain objects constantly phasing in and out of existence (but their hitboxes are always present)?",

    }, {
      "text": "**Examining the Glitch**\n\nI\u0027m currently focused on the user\u0027s Terraria visual issue. I\u0027ve analyzed the request and noted the object phasing problem, which is interesting because the hitboxes remain, so the game is *tracking* the objects. Screenshots were provided, and are being used to try and determine the cause of the problem.\n\n\n**Investigating the Mods**\n\nI\u0027ve examined the screenshots and the user\u0027s mod list. The visual issue with missing leaves strongly suggests a rendering conflict, possibly due to a performance optimization mod or conflicting visual mods. I\u0027m focusing on their mod list now, specifically looking for mods that could affect graphics rendering or tile loading, in an attempt to isolate the source of the glitch.\n\n\n**Pinpointing Likely Conflicts**\n\nI\u0027m now zeroing in on \"Nitrate,\" as it\u0027s known to create visual glitches, especially in conjunction with large content mods. The user\u0027s mod list includes several visual mods, and while \"Luminance\" is interesting, \"Nitrate\" is specifically an engine rewrite/optimizer, and is highly likely the source of the issues. The combination of performance-focused mods with large content mods like Calamity, Infernum, and Fargo\u0027s is a common culprit.\n\n\n**Confirming Initial Hypothesis**\n\nI\u0027ve confirmed my initial suspicion. The \"Nitrate\" mod is indeed a performance optimization tool, specifically targeting Terraria\u0027s tile rendering. My search revealed that the mod significantly alters the internal engine to improve frame rates, which should be very useful for those users.\n\n\n**Pinpointing the Culprit**\n\nI\u0027ve determined Nitrate is the prime suspect. Reviewing the user\u0027s modlist, it\u0027s present, and my research confirms its rendering optimizations can lead to this visual glitch. The experimental options likely trigger the \"blocks phasing\" issue. I also checked potential conflicts, but Nitrate is the key cause, and the answer will target this.\n\n\n**Offering the Solution**\n\nI\u0027m now formulating the solution for the user. I\u0027ll guide them to the `Mod Configuration` menu to find and disable Nitrate\u0027s \"Experimental Tile Rendering\" setting. If that doesn\u0027t work, I\u0027ll advise a full disable of Nitrate and a game reload as the next step. As a final resort, I\u0027ll identify other potential visual strain mods like Fargo\u0027s and Calamity Infernum, and consider Luminance conflicts, if necessary.\n\n\n",

      "text": "Based on your screenshots and your mod list, the visual glitching you are experiencing (where blocks visually disappear but their hitboxes remain) is almost certainly being caused by the **Nitrate** mod. \n\nNitrate is a performance optimization mod that heavily modifies Terraria\u0027s internal tile-rendering engine to increase your FPS. However, because it aggressively stops rendering blocks it thinks you can\u0027t see (culling), it often bugs out—especially when paired with massive content mods like Calamity and Fargo\u0027s—causing blocks to phase in and out of existence.\n\nHere is how you can configure or disable your mods to fix this:\n\n### Option 1: Configure Nitrate (Keep the performance boost)\nIf you want to keep Nitrate for the FPS boost, you can usually fix this by turning off its experimental rendering features.\n1. Open your inventory in-game and go to **Settings**, or go to the Main Menu.\n2. Click on **Mod Configuration**.\n3. Scroll down and click on **Nitrate**.\n4. Look for an option called **Experimental Tile Rendering** (or similar settings related to \"Tile Optimization\" or \"Test block rendering\") and **Disable it**. \n5. Save the configuration and see if the blocks return to normal. *(Note: You may need to reload your world for the changes to apply).*\n\n### Option 2: Disable Nitrate Completely (Safest fix)\nIf changing the configuration doesn\u0027t work, or if the glitches persist, your best bet is to just turn the mod off entirely. \n1. Go to the Terraria Main Menu.\n2. Click on **Manage Mods**.\n3. Scroll down your list, find **Nitrate**, and click the **Disable** button.\n4. Click **Reload Mods**. \n*Your FPS might drop slightly, but your blocks will render completely normally again.*\n\n### Secondary Culprits (If the issue persists)\nIf you disable Nitrate and are still getting visual glitches, look into these mods next:\n*   **Luminance:** This is a visual/lighting library mod (required by Infernum). Sometimes its custom shaders can conflict with Terraria\u0027s base lighting. Try going into Terraria\u0027s base Video Settings and changing your **Lighting** from \"Color\" to \"White\" or \"Retro\" to see if it forces the blocks to render properly.\n*   **Fargo\u0027s Mutant/Souls Mod:** Fargo\u0027s adds a lot of screen-clearing visual effects. Check the Fargo\u0027s Mod Configuration and look for settings that reduce particles or visual clutter.",

      "tokenCount": 539,
      "parts": [{
        "text": "Based on your screenshots and your mod list, the"
      }, {
        "text": " visual glitching you are experiencing (where blocks visually disappear but their hitboxes remain) is almost certainly being caused by the"
      }, {
        "text": " **Nitrate** mod. \n\nNitrate is a performance optimization mod that heavily modifies Terraria\u0027s internal tile"
      }, {
        "text": "-rendering engine to increase your FPS. However, because it aggressively stops rendering blocks it thinks you can\u0027t see (culling),"
      }, {
        "text": " it often bugs out—especially when paired with massive content mods like Calamity and Fargo\u0027s—causing blocks to phase"
      }, {
        "text": " in and out of existence.\n\nHere is how you can configure or disable your mods to fix this:\n\n### Option"
      }, {
        "text": " 1: Configure Nitrate (Keep the performance boost)\nIf you want to keep Nitrate for the FPS boost, you can usually"
      }, {
        "text": " fix this by turning off its experimental rendering features.\n1. Open your inventory in-game and go to **Settings**,"
      }, {
        "text": " or go to the Main Menu.\n2. Click on **Mod Configuration**.\n3. Scroll down and click on **Nitrate"
      }, {
        "text": "**.\n4. Look for an option called **Experimental Tile Rendering** (or similar settings related to \"Tile Optimization\" or \"Test"
      }, {
        "text": " block rendering\") and **Disable it**. \n5. Save the configuration and see if the blocks return to normal. *("
      }, {
        "text": "Note: You may need to reload your world for the changes to apply).*\n\n### Option 2: Disable Nitrate Completely"
      }, {
        "text": " (Safest fix)\nIf changing the configuration doesn\u0027t work, or if the glitches persist, your best bet is to"
      }, {
        "text": " just turn the mod off entirely. \n1. Go to the Terraria Main Menu.\n2. Click on **"
      }, {
        "text": "Manage Mods**.\n3. Scroll down your list, find **Nitrate**, and click the **Disable** button."
      }, {
        "text": "\n4. Click **Reload Mods**. \n*Your FPS might drop slightly, but your blocks will render completely normally again"
      }, {
        "text": ".*\n\n### Secondary Culprits (If the issue persists)\nIf you disable Nitrate and are still getting visual glitches, look into"
      }, {
        "text": " these mods next:\n*   **Luminance:** This is a visual/lighting library mod (required by Infernum)."
      }, {
        "text": " Sometimes its custom shaders can conflict with Terraria\u0027s base lighting. Try going into Terraria\u0027s base Video Settings and changing"
      }, {
        "text": " your **Lighting** from \"Color\" to \"White\" or \"Retro\" to see if it forces the blocks to render"
      }, {
        "text": " properly.\n*   **Fargo\u0027s Mutant/Souls Mod:** Fargo\u0027s adds a lot of screen"
      }, {
        "text": "-clearing visual effects. Check the Fargo\u0027s Mod Configuration and look for settings that reduce particles or visual clutter."
      }, {
